holidays.name: International Joke Day
holidays.description: Kick off the second half of the year with a groan. Today is for swapping puns, dad jokes, knock-knocks and your best punchlines with friends, coworkers and strangers. Bad jokes are welcome, and the worse they are, the better they land.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular way to start July with a laugh.
holidays.funFact: One of the oldest jokes on record is a Sumerian proverb from around 1900 BCE. It is usually cited as a gag about bodily noises, so toilet humor goes back a very long way.

holidays.name: National Gingersnap Day
holidays.description: This day honors the spicy, crunchy molasses cookie that snaps when you bite it. Dunk one in coffee or milk, or crumble it over ice cream. Bake a batch and let the warm smell of ginger and cloves fill the kitchen, even in the middle of summer.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a cookie with centuries of history in European baking traditions.
holidays.funFact: Ginger-flavored baked treats go back to medieval Europe, and gingerbread was a fairground favorite long before it became a Christmas tradition.

holidays.name: International Chicken Wing Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy the saucy, finger-licking snack, whether you like yours mild, atomic, dry-rubbed or smothered in blue cheese. Napkins are mandatory, and so is debating the best flavor.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the wing's rise from a throwaway cut to a bar-food superstar.
holidays.funFact: Buffalo wings are traditionally credited to the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York, in 1964. Wings were once considered scraps, and now Americans eat billions of them during football season alone.
